html:
The Kurykans were a Turkic tribe of the Tiele group who lived around Lake Baikal in southern Siberia from about the 500s. Chinese sources call them Guligan, and the Old Turkic Orkhon inscriptions name them as Quriqan.

They came from the Yenisei region. They bred horses and cattle, farmed a little and worked iron, and they are linked with the Kurumchi archaeological culture of the Baikal area. They lived on the far edge of the steppe empires of the Türks and then the Uyghurs.

Many scholars think the Kurykans were among the ancestors of the Yakuts, or Sakha, who later moved north along the Lena River.
